title: Duke Energy Foundation commits $50,000 to help Florida families in need this holiday season
summary: With the holiday season fast approaching, the Duke Energy Foundation is committing $50,000 to seven organizations helping Central Florida and Tampa Bay area families access safe, affordable housing, nutritious food, financial counseling and other necessities.
body_markdown:
ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. – With the holiday season fast approaching, the Duke Energy Foundation is committing $50,000 to seven organizations helping Central Florida and Tampa Bay area families access safe, affordable housing, nutritious food, financial counseling and other necessities.


**Our view:**


“It’s incredibly important to all of us at Duke Energy that our impact in the communities we serve goes beyond providing reliable power,” said **Melissa Seixas, Duke Energy Florida state president** . “That’s why, together with the Duke Energy Foundation, we’ve provided roughly $18 million to help meet Florida families’ essential needs over the last decade, and it’s why we continue to support such life-changing work today. We want to help our customers thrive.”


**High-impact investments:**


- Through a $10,000 grant, **East Pasco Meals on Wheels** will update its Feeding You With Love food pantry to include adequate shade, cooling, security and traffic safety infrastructure, helping protect both volunteers and clients as demand for food assistance continues to grow.


- **Empowered of Central Florida** will leverage a $15,000 grant to expand its Rolling Rock mobile outreach program to new schools, ensuring more vulnerable students and families receive school supplies, clothing, hygiene products, food and more.


- A $5,000 grant will support **Find, Feed & Restore’s** efforts to open Lake County’s first transitional housing program where women with children fleeing domestic violence can heal and regain self-sufficiency at no cost.


- **Hearts, Hands and Hope** will use a $5,000 grant to continue offering weekly food distributions, as well as healthcare services and workforce development opportunities, for thousands of Seminole County residents.


- With a $5,000 grant, **HOPE Helps Inc.** will provide one-on-one counseling to help individuals and families across Central Florida create personalized financial plans, including guidance on budgeting, saving and managing debt.


- **The Neighborhood Center of South** **Lake** will direct a $5,000 grant to its School Break Food Program, which distributes 10 meals and one snack to students for every week schools are closed during the holidays.


- A $5,000 grant will enable **The Neighborhood Center of West Volusia** to make critical repairs and upgrades to its transitional housing facilities, reducing long-term operational costs and preserving an affordable option for community members facing financial instability.


**Positive response:** ****


- “Duke Energy's partnership with our food pantry reflects a shared commitment to building a stronger, safer community,” said **Beth Aker, East Pasco Meals on Wheels director** . “This collaboration demonstrates how community partnerships can create meaningful, long-term benefits for local families while supporting the volunteers and staff who make our mission possible.”


- “Duke Energy’s support is more than a grant – it’s an investment in the communities we both serve,” said **Troy S. Weaver, Empowered of Central Florida executive director** . “Together, we are giving more students access to the resources they need to succeed while helping them see a brighter future for themselves.”


- “This partnership will help turn fear into safety, uncertainty into stability and hope into a future filled with possibilities,” said **Brian K. Broadway, Find, Feed & Restore founder and CEO** . “We are deeply grateful to Duke Energy for believing in our mission and helping us ensure no one in our community flees the hands of abuse just to run into the arms of homelessness.”


- “When we started Hearts, Hands and Hope 10 years ago, Duke Energy was one of the first to step up and support us. That kind of early belief in a small, growing organization makes all the difference,” said **Michelle Wilson, Hearts, Hands and Hope founder and president** . “Our continued partnership means more children in Central Florida go to school with full stomachs and a real chance to focus on learning, not hunger.”


- “Our partnership with Duke Energy comes at a pivotal moment for Seminole County families facing rising costs of living,” said **HOPE Helps Inc. CEO Joan Faulkner** . “This commitment enables us to deliver hands-on financial education and one-on-one support, giving individuals the resources they need to break cycles of debt and achieve lasting self-sufficiency.”


- “Because of Duke Energy's support, 500 children will have nutritious meals during a week of school break, giving them the food they need to stay healthy, energized and ready to learn,” said **The Neighborhood Center of South Lake chief advancement officer Beth Ann Carr** . “Together, we’re not just putting food on the table; we’re helping families feel supported and giving children the opportunity to succeed.”


- “With this support, we can do more than address an immediate housing crisis – we can restore hope and create a pathway toward long-term stability for vulnerable families in our community,” said **The Neighborhood Center of West Volusia CEO Savannah-Jane Griffin** . “We are incredibly grateful that Duke Energy recognizes safe, affordable housing is foundational to strong families and thriving communities.”


**Duke Energy Foundation**
Duke Energy Foundation provides more than $30 million annually in philanthropic support to meet the needs of communities where Duke Energy customers live and work. The Foundation is funded by Duke Energy shareholders.


**Duke Energy Florida**
Duke Energy Florida, a subsidiary of Duke Energy, owns 12,500 megawatts of energy capacity, supplying electricity to 2 million residential, commercial and industrial customers across a 13,000-square-mile service area in Florida.


**Duke Energy**
Duke Energy (NYSE: DUK), a Fortune 150 company headquartered in Charlotte, N.C., is one of America’s largest energy holding companies. The company’s electric utilities serve 8.7 million customers in North Carolina, South Carolina, Florida, Indiana, Ohio and Kentucky, and collectively own 55,700 megawatts of energy capacity. Its natural gas utilities serve 1.6 million customers in North Carolina, South Carolina, Ohio and Kentucky.


Duke Energy is executing an energy modernization strategy, keeping customer value at the forefront as it invests in electric grid upgrades and efficient generation resources to strengthen the system and serve growing energy needs.
